review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of gradChiTilde, chiGradG, gradG and gradMatrix. I grepped the AnomalousDiffusion tree for places that unfold these definitions. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about how the simplifier behaves. I did not check whether a Matrix.mulVec_apply-style lemma for Fin 2 already exists in Mathlib. The remaining uncertainty is whether the proposed simp lemmas would loop or clash with existing simp sets. The proposals are plain unfoldings of non-recursive definitions, so a loop looks unlikely.

findings.problem: The `hselected` step handles the 2×2 component expansion with an ad hoc simp set. It unfolds `chiGradG`, `gradG`, `Matrix.mulVec`, `dotProduct`, `Matrix.vecHead` and `Matrix.vecTail`, and adds `Fin.sum_univ_two` and `mul_add`. No component-level simp lemmas exist for `chiGradG` or for `gradMatrix`/`gradG` entries. `chiGradG` is a bare `fun i => ∑ j, …` definition, and `gradG` is `Matrix.of fun i j => spaceGrad …`. So every user has to unfold these and re-derive the entries through low-level `Matrix.of` and `vecHead` simp forms. The same `chiGradG` unfolding is repeated by hand elsewhere, for example in `tf_chiGradG_eq` and `sa_chiGradG_eq_hessian`.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definitions in Terms.lean, add `@[simp]` component lemmas such as `chiGradG_apply : chiGradG I hΦ m κ T k t x i = ∑ j, I.chiTilde hΦ m κ k t x j * gradG I hΦ m T (lIdx β I.Λ m k) t x i j`. Add `gradG_apply` and `gradMatrix_apply` in the same way, giving `gradMatrix Χ x i j = spaceGrad (fun y => Χ y j) x i`. Then this call becomes `simpa [S, S₀, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two, …]` without unfolding the project definitions, and other files can reuse the same lemmas.
findings.benefit: Callers get a stable, intentional normal form for entries of these matrices and vectors. They no longer rely on unfolding definitions, which is fragile if a definition changes, and the long simp list shrinks.

findings.problem: `gradChiTilde` is a plain abbreviation for `gradMatrix (I.chiTilde …) x`. There is no simp or equation lemma for it, so the proof passes `gradChiTilde` as a simp argument. This happens at line 90 and again at line 131. The same ad hoc unfolding appears in `ResidualPointwiseConstructor.lean` (`simpa [correctorFlux, gradChiTilde, l]`) and in `CorrectorDiffusionExpansion.lean` (`dsimp [correctorFlux, gradChiTilde, …]`). Statements in this file mix `gradChiTilde` and `gradMatrix (I.chiTilde …)`. The `hvec` and `hcore` steps use `gradMatrix`, while `hlocal` uses `gradChiTilde`. As a result, every bridge between the two forms needs a manual `simpa [gradChiTilde]`.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form and record it. Either make `gradChiTilde` reducible (`abbrev`), or add `@[simp] theorem gradChiTilde_eq : gradChiTilde I hΦ m κm k t x = gradMatrix (I.chiTilde hΦ m κm k t) x := rfl`, with the `gradMatrix` form as the canonical target. Then drop the explicit `gradChiTilde` arguments from the `simpa` calls here and in the files listed above.
findings.benefit: Terms with `gradChiTilde` and terms with `gradMatrix (I.chiTilde …)` normalize to the same expression automatically. This removes repeated `simpa [gradChiTilde]` bridging in the downstream corrector and flux files.
